flags: PayPal announced a strategic reorganization of its business and executive leadership team expected to deliver at least $1.5 billion in gross annualized run-rate savings.

Management implemented a global workforce reduction to simplify operations by removing organizational layers and increasing spans of control, resulting in restructuring charges of $152 million and expected annualized employee-related cost savings of approximately $340 million.

PayPal recorded net losses and impairments on strategic investments that drove other income (expense), net to (240) (table in millions) compared with 111 (table in millions) in the prior-year nine-month period, with net losses on strategic investments of 181 (table in millions) in operating cash flow adjustments.
no_value_reason: some filed figures are years older than the latest annual report

business_model.claim: PayPal operates a global, two-sided payments network connecting consumers and merchants across approximately 200 markets.
quotes: We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects consumers and merchants with 439 million active accounts across approximately 200 markets as of December 31, 2025.

business_model.claim: To consumers, PayPal provides digital wallets, person-to-person transfers, branded payment cards, cryptocurrency trading, and buy-now-pay-later and installment credit products.
quotes: We provide consumers with digital wallets and other solutions that allow them to shop and pay with PayPal and Venmo—both online and in-person—manage their finances (including saving and buying and selling cryptocurrencies), and send and receive money between friends and family.
Our consumer credit offerings include our BNPL products in the U.S., Germany, France, United Kingdom (“U.K.”), and Australia, among other markets, and in Japan through our Paidy brand.

business_model.claim: To large enterprises and small and medium businesses, PayPal sells online branded checkout, unbranded payment processing, point-of-sale solutions, payouts, risk tools, and merchant financing.
quotes: We provide large enterprises and small and medium businesses with online branded checkout solutions, including PayPal and Venmo; online unbranded payments processing; PayPal buy now, pay later (“BNPL”) solutions; in-person point of sale solutions; business financing; payouts capabilities; and risk tools.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1 Business and Item 7 MD&A.
business_model.claim: PayPal earns its primary revenues from transaction fees based on payment volume, alongside fees for currency conversion, cross-border transactions, instant transfers, and cryptocurrency trading.
quotes: We earn revenues primarily by charging fees for completing payment transactions for our customers and other payment-related services, which are typically based on the volume of activity processed on our payments platform.
Transaction revenues: Net transaction fees charged to merchants and consumers on a transaction basis based on the TPV completed on our payments platform.

business_model.claim: PayPal also earns other value-added services revenue from partnerships, credit-program revenue sharing, interest and fees on loans receivable, interest on assets underlying customer balances, and referral, subscription, and gateway fees.
quotes: Revenues from other value added services: Net revenues derived primarily from revenue earned through partnerships, referral fees, subscription fees, gateway fees, and other services we provide to our consumers and merchants.
We also earn revenues from interest and fees earned on our portfolio of loans receivable, and interest earned on certain assets underlying customer balances.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 7 MD&A and 3Q 2026 earnings release.
business_model.claim: Transaction revenue growth correlates with total payment volume and payment transactions, with TPV rising 6% to $487.1 billion across 6.8 billion transactions and 440 million active accounts in the third quarter.
quotes: As our transaction revenue growth is typically correlated with TPV growth and the number of payment transactions completed on our payments platform, management uses these metrics to gain insights into the scale and strength of our payments platform, the engagement level of our customers, and underlying activity and trends which may be indicators of current and future performance.
Total payment volume (“TPV”) increased 6% to $487.1 billion; 7% FXN.
Payment transactions increased 7% to 6.8 billion.
Active accounts increased 0.6% to 440 million.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 7 MD&A and 10-Q Item 2 MD&A.
business_model.claim: Net revenues also depend on product, merchant, and geographic mix, cross-border share, outstanding loans, and foreign exchange movements, with approximately 42% of net revenues generated outside the U.S.
quotes: We generated approximately 42% of our net revenues from customers domiciled outside of the U.S. in both the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.
Transaction revenues growth was lower than the growth in TPV in 2025 due primarily to changes in product mix, merchant mix, and unfavorable impact from foreign exchange hedging activities.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-Q income statement and 10-K Item 7 MD&A.
business_model.claim: Transaction expense is PayPal's largest operating cost at 12,798 out of 21,302 in total operating expenses (table in millions), driven by TPV, processor fees, and funding mix.
quotes: Transaction expense is primarily composed of the costs we incur to accept a customer’s funding source of payment.

The cost of funding a transaction with a credit or debit card is generally higher than the cost of funding a transaction from a bank or through internal sources such as a PayPal or Venmo account balance or our consumer credit products.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-Q income statement and 10-K Item 7 MD&A.
business_model.claim: Transaction and credit losses cover customer protection programs, fraud, chargebacks, and expected credit losses on consumer and merchant loans, totaling 1,161 (table in millions) over nine months.
quotes: Transaction losses include the expense associated with our customer protection programs, fraud, and chargebacks.
Credit losses include the current expected credit losses associated with our consumer and merchant loans receivable portfolio.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-Q income statement and 10-Q Item 2 MD&A.
business_model.claim: PayPal also incurs technology, sales and marketing, administrative, customer support, and restructuring costs, and is executing a reorganization targeting at least $1.5 billion in gross annualized run-rate savings.
quotes: This strategic reorganization and business simplification program, which will focus on realigning our operating structure and accelerating the adoption of artificial intelligence and automation across the Company, is expected to deliver at least $1.5 billion in gross annualized run-rate savings over the next two to three years.

As part of this program, during the third quarter of 2026 management implemented a global workforce reduction to simplify our operations by removing organizational layers across the Company and increasing spans of control (the “3Q 2026 Plan”) resulting in restructuring charges of $152 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026.

competitive_position.claim: PayPal operates a global, two-sided network connecting consumers and merchants with 439 million active accounts across approximately 200 markets as of December 31, 2025, rising 0.6% to 440 million active accounts in the third quarter of 2026.
quotes: We operate a global, two-sided network at scale that connects consumers and merchants with 439 million active accounts across approximately 200 markets as of December 31, 2025.
Active accounts increased 0.6% to 440 million.

competitive_position.claim: PayPal processed $1.79 trillion of TPV across 25.4 billion payment transactions in 2025, and in the third quarter of 2026 TPV rose 6% year over year to $487.1 billion across 6.8 billion payment transactions.
quotes: In 2025, we processed $1.79 trillion of total payment volume (“TPV”), an increase of 7% compared to 2024, and 25.4 billion payment transactions, a decrease of 4% compared to 2024.
Total payment volume (“TPV”) increased 6% to $487.1 billion; 7% FXN.
Payment transactions increased 7% to 6.8 billion.

competitive_position.claim: Management identifies its two-sided data, trusted PayPal and Venmo brands, platform-agnostic architecture, and buyer and seller protection programs as core competitive advantages.
quotes: Our relationship on both sides of a transaction enables us to utilize data to innovate and offer unique product experiences designed to remove friction, drive sales, and enhance shopping experiences.
We have built well-recognized and trusted brands, including PayPal and Venmo.
These seamless experiences reduce cart abandonment and drive higher conversion rates for merchants.

competitive_position.claim: PayPal's product suite spans branded checkout, unbranded processing, P2P transfers, BNPL, consumer and merchant financing, and other value-added services, with other value-added services revenue increasing 14% in 2025.
quotes: We provide large enterprises and small and medium businesses with online branded checkout solutions, including PayPal and Venmo; online unbranded payments processing; PayPal buy now, pay later (“BNPL”) solutions; in-person point of sale solutions; business financing; payouts capabilities; and risk tools.

Revenues from other value added services increased $419 million, or 14%, in 2025 compared to 2024 due primarily to an approximately $350 million increase in interest and fee revenue earned from our loans receivable portfolios as well as an increase of approximately $160 million from revenue earned from an independent chartered financial institution (“partner institution”).

competitive_position.claim: PayPal maintains substantial international reach, generating approximately 43% of net revenues from customers outside the U.S. in 2025 and approximately 42% in both the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.
quotes: In 2025 and 2024, we generated approximately 43% of our net revenues from customers domiciled outside of the U.S. compared to 42% in 2023.
We generated approximately 42% of our net revenues from customers domiciled outside of the U.S. in both the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

competitive_position.claim: Despite shifting Braintree toward profitable growth in 2025, PayPal's GAAP operating margin contracted from 18.1% in the third quarter of 2025 to 16.3% in the third quarter of 2026 due to higher transaction expenses and restructuring charges.
quotes: The increase in TPV for Braintree products and services despite a decline in the number of payment transactions is due to our strategic shift as we focus on profitable growth.

Our operating margin declined, reflecting the unfavorable impact of transaction expense growth and the increase in restructuring and other expenses, partially offset by the decline in transaction and credit losses.
GAAP operating margin contracted 173 basis points to 16.3%; non-GAAP operating margin expanded 16 basis points to 18.8%.

competitive_position.claim: PayPal holds $15.1 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and investments against $13.5 billion of debt as of September 30, 2026, and generated 4,709 (table in millions) in operating cash flow during the nine months ended September 30, 2026.
quotes: Cash, cash equivalents, and investments totaled $15.1 billion as of September 30, 2026.
Debt totaled $13.5 billion as of September 30, 2026.
On a trailing 12-month basis, returned $6.0 billion to stockholders by repurchasing approximately 117 million shares of common stock.

competitive_position.claim: PayPal faces intense competition across physical and electronic payments from banks, card networks and processors, card-on-file services, digital wallets, BNPL providers, real-time payment systems, P2P and remittance providers, cryptocurrencies, stablecoins, and cash.
quotes: The global payments industry is highly competitive, dynamic, innovative, and subject to regulatory scrutiny and oversight.

Competition also may intensify as new competitors emerge, businesses combine or enter into new partnerships, and established companies in other segments expand to become competitive with various aspects of our business.

competitive_position.claim: Rapid technological shifts—including browser card storage, tokenization, real-time payments, distributed ledgers, generative AI, and autonomous AI agents—threaten to make PayPal's products obsolete, while competitors and other third parties could restrict access to key technologies.
quotes: We expect that new technologies applicable to the industries in which we operate, including the development, adoption, and use of generative AI technologies and autonomous AI agents, will continue to emerge and may be superior to, or render obsolete, the technologies we currently use in our products and services.
We rely in part on third parties, including some of our competitors, for the development of and access to new or evolving technologies.
In addition, third parties may deploy AI technologies in a manner that reduces customer demand for our products and services.

competitive_position.claim: Hostile actors target PayPal with cyberattacks and AI-enabled threats, and past or future breaches of customer or payment card data could cause loss of customer confidence, brand harm, remediation expenses, and regulatory penalties.
quotes: We believe that hostile actors, who may comprise individuals, coordinated groups, sophisticated organizations, or nation-state supported entities, may target PayPal due to our name, brand recognition, types of data (including sensitive payments- and identity-related data) that customers provide to us, and the widespread adoption and use of our products and services.
We have experienced, and may experience in the future, breaches involving customer information for which we have notified, and may notify, regulators, customers and other third parties.

competitive_position.claim: System failures, coding errors, and third-party cloud or data-center outages threaten service reliability and trust, illustrated by an August 2025 update error in Germany that triggered fraudulent transactions and protection-program losses.
quotes: For example, in August 2025, PayPal experienced a temporary service disruption triggered by a coding error in a system update, which primarily impacted a limited number of customers and partners in Germany.
In connection with this disruption, we experienced some fraudulent transaction activity for a limited time period.

competitive_position.claim: Complex, evolving global regulation of payments, lending, privacy, and crypto—including the GENIUS Act and supervision by the ECB, FCA, and MAS—imposes compliance costs and limits expansion, with customers in only about half of PayPal's approximately 200 markets able to receive payments.
quotes: While we currently allow our customers to send payments from approximately 200 markets, we allow customers in only approximately half of those markets (including the U.S.) to also receive payments, in some cases with significant restrictions on the manner in which customers can hold balances or withdraw funds.

Additionally, we are a digital asset service provider under the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act of 2025 (the “GENIUS Act”), which subjects us to obligations relating to our cryptocurrency business and may affect the competitive landscape for payment stablecoins.

competitive_position.claim: Cryptocurrency and PYUSD stablecoin offerings expose PayPal to third-party custodian and issuer risks, including uncertain treatment of custodied digital assets in a custodian bankruptcy.
quotes: In the event of a custodian’s bankruptcy, the lack of precedent and the highly fact-dependent nature of the determination could delay or preclude the return of custodied cryptocurrency assets to us or to our customers.

competitive_position.claim: Macroeconomic pressures from tariffs, inflation, international conflicts, and interest rates threaten consumer spending and credit quality; transaction and credit losses rose 19% to $1,720 (table in millions) in 2025 before falling to 1,161 (table in millions) in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 from 1,330 (table in millions) a year earlier.
quotes: A deterioration in macroeconomic conditions resulting from uncertainties and effects from tariffs, inflation, international conflicts, and interest rates could continue to increase the risk of lower consumer spending, merchant and consumer bankruptcy, insolvency, business failure, higher credit losses, foreign exchange fluctuations, or other business interruption, which may adversely impact our business.
Transaction and credit losses increased $278 million, or 19%, in 2025 compared to 2024.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P3, P4, and P6.
growth_thesis.claim: Total payment volume (TPV) growth drove net revenue growth of 4% ($1.4 billion) in 2025 on 7% TPV growth, and 2% ($8.6 billion total net revenues) in third-quarter 2026 results on 6% TPV growth.
quotes: Net revenues increased $1.4 billion, or 4%, in 2025 compared to 2024 driven primarily by growth in total payment volume (“TPV”, as defined below under “Key Metrics”) of 7% and an increase in interest and fee revenue earned on our loans receivable portfolio, partially offset by the unfavorable impact of hedging activities.
The increase in net revenues was driven primarily by growth in total payment volume (“TPV”) of 6% and favorable impact from hedging activities.

As our transaction revenue growth is typically correlated with TPV growth and the number of payment transactions completed on our payments platform, management uses these metrics to gain insights into the scale and strength of our payments platform, the engagement level of our customers, and underlying activity and trends which may be indicators of current and future performance.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1, P3, and P4.
growth_thesis.claim: For TPV-driven revenue growth to continue, macroeconomic conditions, consumer spending, digital payment adoption, market share, and product innovation must remain supportive without adverse mix or hedging offsets.
quotes: Our ability to grow revenue is affected by, among other things, the macroeconomic environment and its impact on commerce and economic growth, consumer spending patterns, adoption of digital payment methods, the growth of multiple commerce channels, the growth of mobile devices and commerce and payment applications on those devices, the growth of consumers and merchants globally with internet and mobile access, the pace of transition from cash and checks to digital forms of payment, our share of digital payments, and our ability to innovate and introduce new products, services, and features that consumers and merchants value.

A deterioration in macroeconomic conditions resulting from uncertainties and effects from tariffs, inflation, international conflicts, and interest rates could continue to increase the risk of lower consumer spending, merchant and consumer bankruptcy, insolvency, business failure, higher credit losses, foreign exchange fluctuations, or other business interruption, which may adversely impact our business.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1, P3, and P6.
growth_thesis.claim: PayPal and Venmo products drove approximately $740 million and $340 million in 2025 transaction revenue growth, respectively, supported by P2P user acquisition, while active accounts reached 440 million (up 0.6%) and payment transactions rose 7% to 6.8 billion in third-quarter 2026 results.
quotes: The increase in 2025 was driven primarily by an increase of approximately $740 million and $340 million in revenue from PayPal and Venmo products and services, respectively, which was largely driven by growth in TPV and number of payment transactions, and an increase of approximately $150 million in revenue from Braintree products and services, predominantly attributable to growth in TPV despite a decline in the number of payment transactions over the same period.

P2P is an important source of customer engagement and also serves as a customer acquisition channel that facilitates organic growth by enabling potential users to establish active accounts with PayPal or Venmo at the time they make or receive a P2P payment.
Active accounts increased 0.6% to 440 million.
Payment transactions increased 7% to 6.8 billion.

growth_thesis.claim: Sustaining branded checkout growth requires reducing checkout friction, enhancing rewards, increasing monthly active accounts, and keeping pace with rapid payment and AI technology changes.
quotes: Accelerating growth in our branded checkout business: by improving our user experience, including by reducing friction and enhancing rewards, we will drive consumer selection and increase conversion rates for merchants.
A critical element of our overall growth strategy involves driving an increase in monthly active accounts, which we expect will contribute to growth in payment transactions, TPV, and net revenues.
If we cannot keep pace with rapid technological developments to provide new and innovative products and services, the use of our products and services and, consequently, our revenues, could decline.

growth_thesis.claim: PayPal's strategic shift in Braintree unbranded processing toward profitable growth generated approximately $150 million in incremental 2025 revenue and helped reduce the transaction expense rate from 0.93% in 2024 to 0.89% in 2025.
quotes: The increase in TPV for Braintree products and services despite a decline in the number of payment transactions is due to our strategic shift as we focus on profitable growth.

The decrease in transaction expense rate in 2025 compared to 2024 was primarily attributable to a lower proportion of TPV from Braintree products and services, which generally have higher expense rates than other products and services, and changes in merchant mix.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P3 and P4; transaction expense totals from F2.
growth_thesis.claim: Continued margin-accretive processing growth depends on merchant negotiations and favorable merchant, product, regional, and funding mix to contain transaction expense growth.
quotes: As a result of our stronger focus on profitable growth and ongoing negotiations with merchants, we experienced lower volume and transaction revenue from our Braintree offerings in the first half of 2025 followed by revenue and TPV growth in the second half of 2025.
Our transaction expense rate is impacted by changes in product mix, merchant mix, regional mix, funding mix, and fees paid to payment processors and other financial institutions.
Our operating margin declined, reflecting the unfavorable impact of transaction expense growth.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1 and P3; balance sheet loan figures from F1.
growth_thesis.claim: Revenues from other value added services grew 14% ($419 million) in 2025, led by an approximately $350 million increase in loans receivable interest and fee revenue and an approximately $160 million increase from the credit partner institution.
quotes: Revenues from other value added services increased $419 million, or 14%, in 2025 compared to 2024 due primarily to an approximately $350 million increase in interest and fee revenue earned from our loans receivable portfolios as well as an increase of approximately $160 million from revenue earned from an independent chartered financial institution (“partner institution”).
Our BNPL solutions are embedded into our branded checkout experiences, which can help increase consumer spend and enable merchants to grow sales.

growth_thesis.claim: Continuing credit and other value added services revenue growth requires credit program returns to remain above the partner institution's minimum return threshold without excessive credit losses, interest rate headwinds, or restrictive lending regulations.
quotes: In the event the overall return on the PayPal branded credit programs funded by the partner institution does not meet a minimum rate of return (“minimum return threshold”) in a particular quarter, our revenue share for that period would be zero.

Further, in the event the overall return on the PayPal branded credit programs managed by the partner institution does not meet the minimum return threshold as measured over four consecutive quarters and in the following quarter, we would be required to make a payment to the partner institution, subject to certain limitations.

A deterioration in macroeconomic conditions or other factors beyond those considered in our estimates could result in credit losses that exceed our current estimated credit losses and adversely impact our future operating results.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P4; nine-month restructuring totals from F2.
growth_thesis.claim: PayPal's April 2026 strategic reorganization and business simplification program accelerates AI and automation adoption and targets at least $1.5 billion in gross annualized run-rate savings, with a significant portion to be reinvested into highest-priority growth initiatives.
quotes: In April 2026, the Company announced a strategic reorganization of its business and executive leadership team intended to accelerate execution of its long-term growth priorities, simplify its operating structure, streamline decision-making, and drive innovation.

This strategic reorganization and business simplification program, which will focus on realigning our operating structure and accelerating the adoption of artificial intelligence and automation across the Company, is expected to deliver at least $1.5 billion in gross annualized run-rate savings over the next two to three years.
The Company intends to reinvest a significant portion of these savings back into its highest-priority growth initiatives.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P2 and inferred from the forward-looking program expectations in P4.
growth_thesis.claim: Realizing growth and operating leverage from the strategic reorganization requires successfully executing multi-year simplification and AI initiatives without disruption or ineffective investments.
quotes: Developing and incorporating new technologies into new and existing products and services may require significant investment, take considerable time, and may not ultimately be successful.

While we continue to undertake system upgrades and re-platforming efforts designed to improve the availability, reliability, resiliency, and speed of our platform, these efforts are costly and time-consuming, involve significant technical complexity and risk, may divert our resources from new features and products, and may ultimately not be effective.

growth_thesis.claim: Global and product-line growth depends on maintaining regulatory licenses, complying with evolving payments, stablecoin, and lending rules, and expanding receive-payment capabilities beyond approximately half of PayPal's 200 markets.
quotes: While we currently allow our customers to send payments from approximately 200 markets, we allow customers in only approximately half of those markets (including the U.S.) to also receive payments, in some cases with significant restrictions on the manner in which customers can hold balances or withdraw funds.
These restrictions may limit our ability to grow our business.

As we introduce new products and services and expand into new markets and support new industries and merchants, including through acquisitions, we expect to become subject to additional regulations, restrictions, and licensing requirements.

risks.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A Risk Factors and the 3Q 2026 Form 10-Q Part I Item 2 and Part II Item 1A Risk Factors.
risks.claim: Extensive and evolving global regulation across payments, banking, lending, privacy, and cryptocurrency could result in fines, enforcement actions, restrictions on operations, or loss of required licenses.
quotes: Regulators and legislators globally continue to establish, evolve, and increase their regulatory authority, oversight, and enforcement, and it may be difficult to predict how these may be applied to our business and the way we conduct our operations.

If we fail to comply with applicable laws or regulations required to maintain our licenses, we could be subject to liability and/or additional restrictions, forced to cease doing business with residents of certain states or territories, forced to change our business practices, or required to obtain additional licenses or regulatory approvals, which could impose substantial costs and harm our business.
We believe that our regulatory licenses, which enable us to operate in markets around the world, are a distinct advantage and help support business growth.
We monitor these areas closely and are focused on designing compliant solutions for our customers.

risks.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A and the 3Q 2026 Form 10-Q Part I Item 2 and Part II Item 1A.
risks.claim: Cyberattacks, data security breaches, and system failures or unplanned outages could disrupt services, cause fraud losses, and lead to regulatory penalties, litigation, and reputational harm.
quotes: We have experienced from time to time, and may experience in the future, cybersecurity incidents, including breaches of our security measures, network breaches, and compromise of personally identifiable customer information due to human error, deception, malfeasance, insider threats, system errors, defects, vulnerabilities, or other issues.

For example, in August 2025, PayPal experienced a temporary service disruption triggered by a coding error in a system update, which primarily impacted a limited number of customers and partners in Germany.

Some of our systems, including those of companies that we have acquired, are not fully redundant and any failure of these systems, including due to a catastrophic event, may lead to operational outages or delays.

risks.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A, weighed against reorganization plans in the 3Q 2026 Form 10-Q Item 2 and operating metrics in the 3Q 2026 Form 8-K.
risks.claim: Failure to keep pace with rapid payment technology changes—including real-time payments, tokenization, digital currencies, and autonomous AI agents—could reduce customer demand and erode revenues.
quotes: We expect that new technologies applicable to the industries in which we operate, including the development, adoption, and use of generative AI technologies and autonomous AI agents, will continue to emerge and may be superior to, or render obsolete, the technologies we currently use in our products and services.
In addition, third parties may deploy AI technologies in a manner that reduces customer demand for our products and services.

If we are unable to develop and incorporate new technologies and adapt to technological changes and evolving industry standards in a timely or cost-effective manner, our business, results of operations, or reputation could be harmed.

risks.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors under Cryptocurrency Regulation and Related Risks.
risks.claim: Reliance on third-party custodians for customer cryptocurrency assets and a third-party issuer for the PYUSD stablecoin exposes PayPal to counterparty default, reserve shortfalls, and unsettled bankruptcy treatment.
quotes: We hold our customers’ cryptocurrency assets through one or more third-party custodians.

In the event of a custodian’s bankruptcy, the lack of precedent and the highly fact-dependent nature of the determination could delay or preclude the return of custodied cryptocurrency assets to us or to our customers.

In that event, our claim on behalf of such customers against a custodian’s estate for our customers’ cryptocurrency assets could be treated as a general unsecured claim against the custodian, in which case our customers could seek to hold us liable for any resulting losses.

risks.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 7 and 3Q 2026 Form 10-Q Item 2 under Impact of Foreign Exchange Rates.
risks.claim: Generating approximately 42% of net revenues outside the United States exposes PayPal to currency translation swings, hedging losses, and daily foreign exchange rate-setting risk.
quotes: We generated approximately 42% of our net revenues from customers domiciled outside of the U.S. in both the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.
While we enter into foreign exchange contracts to help reduce the impact on earnings from foreign exchange rate movements, it is impossible to eliminate the total effects of this exposure.

Additionally, in connection with transactions occurring in multiple currencies on our payments platform, we generally set our foreign exchange rates daily and may face financial exposure if we incorrectly set our foreign exchange rates or as a result of fluctuations between setting of foreign exchange rates and timing of transactions.
